Too many useless AI features.
Not enough functionality.
If you want people to pay THAT badly, just charge an upfront fee to download the app.
Not doing so is blatant disrespect and manipulation, neither of which breed customer appreciation or trust.

I would’ve been willing to pay, if I saw that this app was worth it.

So I won’t.

The only reason I’m giving this app 2 stars is because, while it does give you a good amount of free likes, the way they handle people who have already shown interest in you makes absolutely no sense.

If someone views your profile, you would think the app would at least let you like them back or send them a message. Instead, you have to pay $20 for one week just to interact with someone who may already be interested in you. You can use your free likes to like random profiles, but if someone has actually taken the time to view your profile, suddenly you have to pay to do anything about it.

That’s what I don’t understand. Why give users free likes if you can’t use them to connect with people who are already showing some interest? I could pay $20, message someone, and they might not even respond. That’s a pretty ridiculous price just for the possibility of making a connection.

I understand apps need to make money, and I’m not against premium features, but charging $20 just to message someone who has already viewed your profile feels excessive. At the very least, users should be able to like or message someone who has viewed their profile without having to pay for a subscription. WEEKLY not monthly WEEKLY!!!!

Right now, it feels less like the app is helping people connect and more like it’s trying to force you into paying just to talk to people who are already interested.

reviews.title: Good for making friends, but not for dating
reviews.text:
I’ve made some friends on here, but the dating aspect really needs some updates. You get shown people who clearly aren’t who you’d be interested in based on what you put into the app for preferences, and similarly people who are way outside of established preferences are allowed to view and message you. For example, I’m a guy and a bunch of men who had “straight” as their preference in their profiles reached out to hit on me. I had put that I was looking for long term, but got shown and liked by a bunch of people looking for something short term. Or, I put in my preferred distance range and was shown people way outside of it, like on the other side of the country. I tried shuffling through hundreds of profiles to try to get the algorithm to work, but it never learned. Then, anyone that actually met my preferences was locked behind a pay wall.

Toss in that the app sends you reminders every 5 minutes that someone liked your profile and that you haven’t read the notification, or compiles them all for yet another notification later even after you’ve sorted through your in app notifications, and it’s a pretty obnoxious experience for dating.

It has the potential to be great, but really needs more work put into it.

reviews.title: Practically Unusable
reviews.text:
I want to like this app, I really do. I even met a partner on here who I dated for a year! However, it’s just unusable! To start, it spans you with notifications. Ever wanted an app to tell you every time someone views your profile? No? Well it’s enabled by default, so if you want to keep your sanity you’d better turn it off. Second, it has these auto messages you can send to start a chat. Don’t want to send them? Well you’d better not leave a match waiting too long or Taimi will send a message without asking. And third, it literally locks you out of liking certain people unless you pay. It’ll show you them all the time, but any attempt to interact with them opens a pay window. Swiping and one of these accounts shows up? Unless you didn’t notice, paywall. It’s insidious. Either these are bots, which is scummy, or these are real accounts for real people that are being used as bait without permission. Have I been used like that? I understand that they need to make money, but they’ve already got adds, limited swipes, a priority message system. What’s the point of locked accounts aside from making you just feel bad?

In short, there’s literally no reason to use Taimi. Save yourself the headache and try literally anything else.

reviews.title: Double Paywall
reviews.text: I’ve been using Taimi for about a week and purchased a subscription because the free version is extremely limited. While I appreciate the app’s design and some of its features, I’m disappointed by what appears to be it’s matching strategy. The app seems to learn your preferences based on the profiles you like and interact with. As it identifies people who appear to be much better matches for you, many of those profiles are locked behind an additional paid “Diamond” feature. In other words, after already paying for a subscription, you’re asked to pay even more just to express interest in some of the people the app itself has determined are your best matches. If that’s how the system works, it seems like double monetization. A paid subscription should include the ability to like and message anyone on the platform who is available to you, not require another purchase for the people you’re most likely to connect with. I’d gladly give it a higher rating if the subscription truly unlocked the full dating experience instead of putting the best potential matches behind another paywall. I don’t recommend this app.

reviews.title: Manipulative, Misleading, and Not Worth It
reviews.text:
Taimi is a deeply cynical app that wraps itself in LGBTQ branding while delivering an experience that feels hollow, manipulative, and exploitative. Instead of feeling like a genuine space for connection, it feels like a polished trap built to keep vulnerable people engaged, disappointed, and paying.

The number of profiles and interactions that seem fake, misleading, or suspicious is honestly insulting. It creates the impression of hope just long enough to keep people swiping, waiting, and spending, while trust disappears almost immediately. Rather than building a real community, it feels like the app feeds off loneliness and sells fantasy back to people at a premium.

That is what makes it so ugly. It is not just a bad app, it feels predatory in spirit. When a platform presents itself as supportive and inclusive but leaves users feeling misled, drained, and used, that is not a technical flaw. That is a character problem.

I would never recommend Taimi. In my view, it feels far more interested in monetizing desperation than creating genuine connection, and that is a terrible look for any app claiming to serve the LGBTQ community. -5 stars
